Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail In 1803, Meriwether Lewis and William Clark embarked on their historic expedition along what we now recognize as the Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail. Stretching roughly 4,900 miles from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, to Astoria, Oregon, this trail traverses 16 states and numerous tribal lands, preserving a crucial chapter in American history. Managed by various federal land management agencies, as well as state, local, tribal, and private organizations, sections of the trail provide visitors with an authentic glimpse into the landscapes encountered by the explorers. Notably, the 2019 John D. Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act expanded the trail by an additional 1,200 miles along the Ohio and Mississippi Rivers, linking Pittsburgh to Wood River, Illinois. One prominent landmark along the route is Pompey’s Pillar National Monument in Montana, where Captain Clark's signature remains engraved—a tangible link to the expedition's passage. pages.text: Lexi Kilfoyl's dominant relief appearance sends Bandits to AUSL Championship Series Skip to Content In a thrilling 11-inning play-in victory over the Portland Cascade on Thursday night to punch their ticket to the AUSL Championship Series against the Utah Talons, the Chicago Bandits got a tremendous performance by right-hander Lexi Kilfoyl. Kilfoyl came on in relief of starter Kat Sandercock in the fifth inning with her team trailing, 3-0. And from there, Kilfoyl was nearly unhittable over seven innings. With the length of a regulation game being seven innings in softball, her appearance was as long as a complete game. Kilfoyl faced 28 batters and yielded just two hits while walking none, hitting a batter and striking out four on an incredible 115 pitches. ATHLETES UNLIMITED SOFTBALL LEAGUE Talons win second straight AUSL title Everything to know about AUSL All-Star Cup Complete AUSL coverage Although Portland scratched across a pair of runs against Kilfoyl, both were unearned. And she did not allow a hit over her final five innings -- Cascade batters were 0-for-23 during that stretch. The clutch performance was reminiscent of some of the greatest -- and longest -- relief appearances in MLB history. And by number of innings and pitches, it would be a rare feat in the Major Leagues. Since 1994, there has only been one instance in the Majors of a relief pitcher going at least seven innings and throwing at least 115 pitches. That was Jordan Lyles for the Rangers against the A’s on Sept. 11, 2020, when he went seven innings and threw exactly 115 pitches.

Close lhirlimann's Diary Capitole du Libre 2026 Posted by lhirlimann on 15 November 2026 in French (Français) . Hier soir, j’ai présenté dans l’amphithéâtre C002 au sein du campus de enseeiht à Toulouse, « Contribuez à OSM ». La bonne surprise fut le taux de remplissage de la salle. J’ai compté plus d’une vingtaine de personnes. La présentation était articulée en deux parties : la première, un tout petit peu de théorie et pas de présentation d’outils ; la deuxième, des démonstrations, des petits trucs faciles pour commencer, puis des trucs plus « grands » (de l’infrastructure). En trente minutes, j’avais plié ma présentation. Il restait vingt-cinq minutes, qui se sont très, très facilement remplies par de très nombreuses questions. Merci au plublic pour ces questions. Merci à l’organisation du Capitole du Libre. La présentation est disponible à https://files.hirlimann.net/talks/cdl2026/ . pages.text: Liam Hendriks wins 2021 AL Reliever of the Year Award Skip to Content CHICAGO -- There's a chance that when he was named the 2021 American League Reliever of the Year, White Sox right-hander Liam Hendriks pumped his fist and let out a yell in celebration. That sort of reaction represented Hendriks’ excitable norm during his first season as the closer for the AL Central champions. Hendriks won the award for the second consecutive year (after taking home the honor as a member of the A’s in 2020), making him the first AL reliever to earn it more than once. L uis Pacheco y Héctor Chaclán , autoridades ancestrales de los 48 Cantones de Totonicapán en 2023, fueron detenidos el 23 de abril de 2025 por su participación en protestas pacíficas. Han sido acusados de terrorismo , asociación ilícita y obstaculización a la acción penal , cargos que podrían implicar décadas de prisión. Amnistía Internacional declaró a Luis y Héctor como presos de conciencia el 6 de mayo de 2026 , porque su detención se basa únicamente en el ejercicio pacífico de sus derechos. Su proceso presenta retrasos e irregularidades, y más de un año después siguen en prisión preventiva. ¿Cómo puedes ayudar? En muchos casos estas organizaciones han desempeñado un papel importante en la transformación democrática de sus países. La OIT está comprometida a promover la libertad sindical en sus actividades, por ejemplo a través de la asesoría a gobiernos sobre legislación laboral, o la formación y capacitación dirigida hacia sindicatos o grupos empleadores. El Comité de libertad sindical de la OIT fue creado en 1951 para examinar los alegatos sobre violaciones a los derechos de organización de trabajadores y empleadores. El Comité es tripartita y maneja casos de todos los Estados miembros de la OIT, aunque no hayan ratificado los Convenios sobre este tema. A través del Comité de libertad sindical y de otros órganos de supervisión la OIT ha defendido con frecuencia los derechos de organizaciones de trabajadores y empleadores. Library and information science is a field of study that encompasses all of the aspects of the creation, organization, documentation, management, communication, and use of recorded information. It is the umbrella term for a wide variety of fields of study and work, including librarianship, information management, knowledge management, archiving, and records management, and is tangential to museum studies. While library science and information science are two separate disciplines, they are interrelated and are often used synonymously. The Zawiya refinery, west of the capital Tripoli, was hit in a drone strike on Monday evening - the third such incident in two days. The National Oil Corporation (NOC) said a tank containing about 4.5m litres of fuel was directly hit, triggering a huge fire that caused it to collapse. It said it was considering suspending operations if the attacks continued. There were no "serious injuries" from the fire, with most patients treated for smoke inhalation, Libya's Ambulance and Emergency Service said on Tuesday. The Zawiya refinery is the largest operational facility in Libya, with an output of 120,000 barrels per day. The NOC condemned similar attacks in past days in Zawiya, including two drone strikes on a naphtha reservoir and a water desalination plant. It called on the authorities to investigate who was behind the violence. The attacks have highlighted continuing instability in Libya, which has been split in two since a civil war broke out after the ousting of former leader Muammar Gaddafi. Just three years ago he was clinging in terror to the roof of a house as the world's deadliest flood this century surged around him. Now the 27-year-old port worker, his wife and two young daughters have been given a new, free, 300-sq-m home in a showcase development commissioned by a son of Khalifa Haftar, the warlord who controls eastern Libya. It is part of a rapid $2bn (£1.5bn) rebuilding of Derna that the powerful Haftar family hope will serve as a model for development throughout Libya, increasing their influence across a country currently split between east and west, with rival governments in charge. The money comes from the state coffers of the oil-rich country, allocated by its parliament. In the darkroom Don't miss... Listen to the audio guide About the exhibition Immerse yourself in bewitching, otherworldly photographs from around the world. See over 200 rare vintage photographic prints up close and discover unusual experiments with darkroom techniques in this exhibition that explores pictorialism – the first international art photography movement. What is pictorialism? At its heart, pictorialism was a declaration: photography is more than just taking a picture, it’s a genuine art form. Beginning in the 1880s, pictorialist photographers worked to create images that were as imaginative, expressive and technically considered as any painting or drawing. They experimented in the darkroom and the studio, out in the city and in their living rooms, crafting images that are full of beauty, mood and aesthetic impact. pages.text: Light pollution is getting worse, and Earth is paying the price | National Geographic By Nadia Drake Photographs by Babak Tafreshi Published April 3, 2019 • 25 min read On a clear night in 1994, an earthquake rumbled beneath Los Angeles and caused a city-wide power outage just before dawn. Startled awake, some residents who had stumbled outside called various emergency centers and a local observatory to report a mysterious cloud overhead. That weird object turned out to be the band of the Milky Way , our home galaxy, which had long been obscured from view by the city’s lights. Arguably, the light bulb is the most transformative invention humans have introduced to this planet. By flicking a switch or pushing a button, we can push back the veil that would naturally shroud our lives each night. Now, we work long after the sun sinks below the horizon. We play games outside until the hours stretch into double digits. We more safely roam city streets after dark. ( Opinion: Bright Nights, Big Problems) The city of Las Vegas dumps an enormous amount of light into its environment, turning the night sky above into a seemingly blank canvas. With their drama and power, it’s no wonder people have infused them with symbolic meaning. They’re associated with mythological deities, such as Zeus and Thor, and even an emoji , in popular culture. By Annie Roth Published November 7, 2019 • 3 min read This story appears in the December 2019 issue of National Geographic magazine. Banana peels and plastic straws are little more than garbage in most of the world. To environmental educator Lillygol Sedaghat , they’re precious commodities. For the past two years, the 27-year-old National Geographic explorer has traveled the globe to advocate for the untapped potential of trash. The linear economy, where resources are turned into disposable products, “is no longer sustainable,” Sedaghat says. pages.text: Limits on Autonomy in Weapon Systems | ICRC Skip to main content Article 02-06-2020 Limits on Autonomy in Weapon Systems Weapons and disarmament Legal review of weapons Conduct of hostilities and protection of civilians Share Share on X Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook There is wide recognition that the need to preserve human control over weapon systems and the use of force in armed conflict will require limits on autonomous weapon systems. This report from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) and the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) offers in-depth analysis of the type and degree of human control that is required to mitigate the risks posed by autonomous weapons. It proposes three types of control measures to reduce or compensate for the unpredictability introduced by autonomous weapons and associated risks for civilians: controls on the weapon's parameters such as types of targets, controls on the environment of use and controls in the form of human supervision. Limits on Autonomy in Weapon Systems: Identifying Practical Elements of Human Control is a comprehensive examination of the specific controls on AWS needed to ensure human control over the use of force, and to address legal, ethical and operational concerns. Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of murdering her three children, will face a retrial next year, a judge has said, after a jury deadlocked last time in a case that gripped the nation. The judge set a trial date for 29 March 2027, though the district attorney did not explicitly say what charges Clancy would face. Prosecutors said they wanted a jury trial, and the defence said they took that to mean Clancy, 36, would again face first-degree murder charges. Copy markdown In this article About linked issues and pull requests You can link an issue to a pull request manually or using a supported keyword in the pull request description, that is, the summary text added by the author when they created the pull request. When you link a pull request to the issue the pull request addresses, collaborators can see that someone is working on the issue. When you merge a linked pull request into the default branch of a repository, its linked issue is automatically closed. For more information about the default branch, see Changing the default branch . Note The special keywords in a pull request description are interpreted only when the pull request targets the repository's default branch. If the pull request targets any other branch , then these keywords are ignored, no links are created, and merging the PR has no effect on the issues.
